title: Locate the anomalous component on a circuit board
data_origin: External research reference. Not captured, owned, or supplied by Weekday.

annotation.note: Binary segmentation version of source annotations. Not a model prediction, confidence heatmap, or generated mask. No multi-class defect id retained in this binary mirror.

task: Anomaly localization: given the PCB image, predict a pixel-level anomaly map; compare against the supplied ground-truth mask.
evaluation_context: This is a test example, not a training-split claim. In the one-class protocol, learn normal appearance from the normal training split, evaluate on held-out normal and anomalous images. A single example cannot establish benchmark performance.
visual_observation: The selected PCB has a visibly bent leftmost pin. Mask marks that pin; bent-pin description is our visual observation, not a preserved multiclass id in this binary file.
attribution: Visual Anomaly (VisA), Yang Zou, Jongheon Jeong, Latha Pemula, Dongqing Zhang, and Onkar Dabeer, SPot-the-Difference Self-Supervised Pre-training for Anomaly Detection and Segmentation, ECCV 2022. CC BY 4.0. Accessed 2026-10-23.
transformations: Extracted exact image and mask bytes from pinned mirror Parquet row, no image re-encoding.
Mirror uses binary mask values 0 and 255 instead of source multiclass ids. Full mirror transformation code not verified.
Any color overlay added on website is a display of the supplied mask, not model inference.
provenance_limit: File names and image/mask dimensions inspected in pinned mirror. Pixel hashes have not been cross-checked against primary S3 tar; do not claim byte identity to original archive.
commercial_display: Dataset license permits sharing/adaptation with attribution and change notice; no endorsement may be implied.
